purpose: Business screen design concept, not implemented application evidence
example: Mixed salon, beauty products and home visits requiring coverage setup
originalPrompt:
Generate exactly ONE polished desktop application screenshot: the finished BUSINESS screen of the existing NEXG merchant workspace. Use the first reference image as authoritative for the exact existing application shell and identity: near-black left sidebar, gold NEXG wordmark, dark-grey rounded selected nav row with a thin gold left edge, warm cream background, white top bar, compact line icons, clean readable sans-serif typography, restrained gold buttons and neutral dividers. Use the second reference for the established white rounded detail panel with close button, compact fields and fixed bottom action area. Neither reference is an edit target; both are style/layout references. Do not use blue sidebars, gradients or a new design language.

Screen image only, landscape about 16:9. No browser chrome, device mockup, external title or explanatory diagram. Everything including the bottom actions fits on a single desktop screen, with readable compact sizing and calm spacing. No giant cards or oversized empty banners. All nine sidebar items appear in this order: Home, Work, Offerings, Availability, Business (selected), Money, Promotions, Insights, Settings. The top bar reads Merchant workspace and has a small Sample preview badge, All locations selector, notifications, Help and NC avatar. The separate Settings screen is visible in navigation. Do NOT put account/security/password preferences, notification preferences, API keys, credential setup, payment setup or ERP controls in the Business screen.

This is one realistic populated Business design concept, using a fictional mixed business Nairobi Collective with salon services, beauty product sales, and a home-visit activity still awaiting setup. It demonstrates configurable activities in one portal. Main title 'Business', secondary text 'Nairobi Collective'. At top show a compact single-line summary with independent labels 'Business approved', '2 configured activities', '1 setup task'. Below it a horizontal section navigation: Profile, Activities & setup (selected), Locations & coverage, Team, Documents, Customer feedback. These tabs have one clear selected state. Do not duplicate their entire contents simultaneously.

Main content below: left about 62%, right about 38%. Left: heading 'Your activities', small search input, a quiet '+ Add activity' gold button. A compact white table with columns Activity, Where it happens, Setup. Three rows: 'Salon services' / 'Westlands studio' / green 'Configured' (selected row warm gold tint); 'Beauty product sales' / 'Westlands · pickup & delivery' / green 'Configured'; 'Home visits' / 'Customer location' / amber 'Coverage needed'. Each row has its own small appropriate line icon and chevron. Make it clear that candidate services do not activate by category alone.

Below the activity table use a modest white card 'Complete setup' with a single useful row: 'Home visits: define your service area' and a small action 'Set coverage'. Supporting sentence 'Home visits remain unavailable until setup is complete.' Then a small concise context card or footer 'Configured activities determine the relevant fields, fulfilment and workflow across your workspace.' Do not add performance charts, financial summaries or generic onboarding tasks.

Right: an existing-style white rounded side panel titled 'Salon services' with a close X. A small green Configured badge and 'Westlands studio' beneath. Show neat labelled, populated setup facts rather than a huge form: 'Service location' = 'At the merchant venue'; 'Scheduled appointments' = 'Enabled · optional'; 'Location' = 'Westlands studio'; 'Team & resources' = '2 linked service providers'; 'Schedule source' = 'NEXG booking'; 'Fulfilment' = 'At the venue'. These are separate from products and home visits. Add a subdued source line 'Current configuration · Revision 12'. A compact informational note says 'Changes affect future work. Existing bookings retain their agreed setup.' Fixed panel footer has a secondary 'Preview configuration' button and gold primary 'Edit setup'. Do not invent verified licences, document approvals, stock numbers, live transactions or system permissions.

Use concise exact text and ensure no duplicate sections, no nonsensical repeated labels, no fake switches that mark approval or verification. Preserve the existing application's visual family from the references. Output one seamless Business screen, not multiple screens or a collage.
